title: Praline chocolate squares
subtitle: dark chocolate squares layered with crisp almond praline and cut into neat pieces
excerpt: Praline chocolate squares are made by spreading tempered dark chocolate into a thin layer, topping it with crushed caramelised almond praline, and covering with a second layer of chocolate. Once set and cut into squares, each piece has a snapping chocolate shell and a sweet, crunchy praline centre. The praline can be made several days ahead.
sourceNotes: Praline originated in France, with the name attributed to the household of the Marechal du Plessis-Praslin in the seventeenth century. Chocolate and praline combinations became a staple of European confectionery, particularly in Belgian and French traditions.

glossaryTerms.definition: Caramelised sugar cooked with nuts, poured flat and left to cool until brittle, then crushed. Used as a filling or topping for chocolates and cakes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. The praline layer stays crisp.

content.text: Praline chocolate squares have a crisp, snapping outer layer and a sweet, crunchy

centre. The praline is made first: almonds cooked in caramelised sugar, poured flat, and left to set until brittle. The crushed praline goes between two thin layers of chocolate. Once set, the slab is cut into even squares with a sharp knife.
Line a baking tray with baking paper. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until lightly golden, about 3 minutes. Set aside.

Put the caster sugar in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat without stirring until it melts into an amber caramel. Swirl the pan rather than stirring once the edges start to colour. When the caramel is dark amber (about 175 to 180 degrees C), add the toasted almonds and swirl to coat.

Pour immediately onto the lined tray and spread in a thin, even layer. Leave to set completely at room temperature, about 20 minutes. Crush the hardened praline into small pieces using a rolling pin or food processor.
Line a shallow 20 cm square tin with baking paper. Melt half the chocolate over a bain-marie and spread into the tin as a thin base layer. Refrigerate for 10 minutes to set.

Scatter the crushed praline evenly over the set chocolate base. Melt the remaining chocolate and pour over the praline layer, spreading to the edges. Scatter flaked salt over the top if using. Refrigerate for 30 to 40 minutes until fully set.
Turn out onto a board and cut into squares using a sharp knife warmed briefly in hot water and dried between cuts. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

attrs.problem: Caramel crystallises and turns grainy instead of running clear
attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the sugar once it begins to melt; agitation causes crystallisation.
attrs.fix: Swirl the pan gently to distribute the heat rather than using a spoon. If it does crystallise, add 2 tablespoons of water and heat again from the start.

attrs.avoid: Avoid cutting before the chocolate is fully set; the layers slide apart.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate for the full time and allow the slab to sit at room temperature for 5 minutes before cutting. Use a knife that is just warm, not hot.
